a line up, or three while the screen scrolls
the PLAs drop the walking routine's return, so the engine neither moves him nor sets him back on a character row
by the way he faces, where the character looked at lies from the screen row under him: $77 (three rows down, a column behind) facing left, $7B (three rows down, three columns on) facing right

object type 15, the level's end boss: a block four sprites across and four rows down (sprites $EC to $FB), drawn by sprites 3 to 6 used again for each row by interrupts of its own. While it is on, the level runs its own sprites ($03ED) and the screen stops scrolling. It falls in from above the screen and then moves at random, across 3 pixels a frame or down 8 lines and up 4. Where a wall stops it, it shakes the screen for 24 frames with a crash, then takes a new way. The hero can ride on its top; inside it he is pushed out to a side or hurt. 1,111 energy; destroyed, it bursts into eleven explosions for 10,000 points
its first frame waits, the object left new, until the hero is on the ground ($29 and $26 zero), not the wheel ($2D), and the fine scroll is at rest ($17 = 4, $16 = 3)

takes the screen over: the level runs its own sprites ($03ED); no scroll ($18, $19), no shaking ($BD16, $BD17); its raster routine $73EB replaces the multiplexer ($071E), the scroll decision at $084D points at the RTS at $085D, $7361 and $6F3B go into the level's frame vectors at $0862 and $0865, and both scroll stages ($0718, $071A) point at the interrupt's exit ($087A)
its first way is down ($BD15 = 1) for 211 frames, with 1,111 energy ($BD18, $BD19 = $0457)

places it by the view's column ($09 less $AA): the left column's X and high bit from $75A0 and $75B8, the other three columns 24 pixels apart, and the four rows at their starting Y from $75E4, the top row above the screen. The third ADC has no CLC before it, so where the second wraps past 255 the right column lands a pixel too far right
removes every object but the boss itself
writes the shown screen's page plus 3 ($0205) into the four STAs of the raster routine, so it sets the sprite pointers at the end of that screen

destroyed: flashes and bursts ($718E)

picks a new way at random: across or up and down by a random bit. The direction is random too, but when it is the one the boss had last, it turns round. Across lasts 7 to 127 frames, up or down 7 to 63, and the other way stops

object type 3, the drip (blue): forms under the ceiling (shapes $98 to $9C, one every 8 frames), falls 4 lines a frame and splashes where it meets a wall (shapes $9D to $A0, one every 4 frames) with the sound $91. Then it forms again where it started. It cannot be shot; touching it hurts the hero, unless he is shielded or the wheel, which bursts it
